transcript.sitrep:
SITUATION (Week 1). A novel respiratory virus has been confirmed in three US cities, with likely undetected spread. Early case reports are alarming but the sample is tiny and biased toward the sickest. You do not yet know the true infection-fatality rate or how transmissible it is. Hospitals in the affected cities report rising admissions. Markets fell 4% on the news. The WHO has called an emergency meeting.

Your health agencies want aggressive early action 'to be safe'; your economic team warns that shutting down on a maybe could be its own catastrophe; governors are looking to you for a lead but guard their authority. Every option has a cost, and you must choose before the data is in. What do you do?

actions.name: surge_testing

params.rationale: We need immediate genomic surveillance and widespread testing to determine true transmissibility and severity before deciding on broader closures.

actions.rationale: We need immediate genomic surveillance and widespread testing to determine true transmissibility and severity before deciding on broader closures.

actions.name: invoke_dpa

params.rationale: We cannot wait for perfect information; we must pre-position PPE, tests, and ventilators now in case this virus is highly severe and transmissible.

actions.rationale: We cannot wait for perfect information; we must pre-position PPE, tests, and ventilators now in case this virus is highly severe and transmissible.

actions.name: fund_vaccine

params.rationale: Getting ahead of this pathogen with a crash vaccine and therapeutics program is essential regardless of how the next few weeks unfold.

actions.rationale: Getting ahead of this pathogen with a crash vaccine and therapeutics program is essential regardless of how the next few weeks unfold.

actions.name: candid_briefings

params.rationale: Americans and markets need steady, honest leadership; transparency now builds trust and compliance for any future measures.

actions.name: mask_mandate

params.rationale: This is a low-cost, high-upside precaution that sets a national standard while we determine how transmissible the virus truly is.

params.rationale: A transparent national data dashboard will give the public, governors, and investors real-time information to make informed decisions.

actions.name: consult_congress

params.rationale: We need to secure emergency funding and statutory authorities now so we are not legally or fiscally constrained if the situation worsens.

actions.name: protect_vulnerable

params.rationale: While we gather data, we should immediately shield nursing homes and high-risk populations, keeping broader society as open as safely possible.

actions.rationale: While we gather data, we should immediately shield nursing homes and high-risk populations, keeping broader society as open as safely possible.

SITUATION (Week 2). Estimated infection index 1.7 (was 1.0 at week 1). Deaths to date: 0.
Economy index 99/100. Public trust 57/100. Hospital strain 2/100. Restriction level 0.5/10.
Vaccine/therapeutics progress: 22/100.
ASSESSMENT (LOW confidence): data remain too thin to pin down severity; estimates span from 'bad flu' to 'catastrophic.'

actions.name: surge_testing

params.rationale: Infection index jumped to 1.7; we urgently need more genomic surveillance and case data to determine whether this is a bad flu or something worse.

actions.rationale: Infection index jumped to 1.7; we urgently need more genomic surveillance and case data to determine whether this is a bad flu or something worse.

params.rationale: While severity is unclear, restricting inbound travel from affected regions can buy us critical time for vaccine and therapeutic development.

DEVELOPMENT: A cluster at a packed event seeds cases in a dozen new states. Pressure to act -- or to stop overreacting -- is intense from all sides.

SITUATION (Week 3). Estimated infection index 2.9 (was 1.0 at week 1). Deaths to date: 0.
Economy index 98/100. Public trust 59/100. Hospital strain 4/100. Restriction level 1.2/10.
Vaccine/therapeutics progress: 43/100.
ASSESSMENT (HIGH confidence): the pathogen is comparable to a severe seasonal flu; transmissibility is very high.
